The present detailed accident report arises out of road accident in which one Harish Salikram Soni aged about 55 years, suffered injuries. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 06.11.2023 upon receipt of Pcr call vide Dd no.11A, Ct. Mohit reached the spot i.e. Archana Red light, Brt road, Greater Kailash-I, where vehicle no.DL-12CR-7508 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) was found in accidental condition. Driver of the offending vehicle had been apprehended and victims were rushed to Aiims Trauma center. Vide Dd No.21A, Mlc no. An Fir No.291/23 was registered u/s 279/337/304A Ipc was registered at Ps Greater Kailash. Police investigated the matter. During investigation, it was revealed by injured Harish that on 06.11.2023 while he was crossing Brt road alongwith 2- 3 other women, at about 7 Am, a gray colour car bearing no.DL-12CR-7508 came from Moolchand side at a very high speed, driven in rash and negligent manner and hit Harish as well as those 2-3 other ladies. All the victims were rushed to Aiims Trauma center in Pcr. The other injured were identified as Rekha Devi, Neeru and Seema Devi. Victims Harish Salikram Soni and Seema Devi sustained simple injuries while victims Rekha Devi and Neeru succumbed to the fatal injury. 4. During investigation, breath analyzer test was conducted on the driver of the offending vehicle wherein breath alcohol 290mg/100ml. was found. The driver could not produce a valid driving licence. Chargesheet u/s 279/337/304-A of Ipc and Mact no.454/2024 Harish Salikram Soni vs. Vinay & ors. Page no . 2 of 20 ss Digitally signed by Charu Charu Date: gupta gupta 2025.12.16 16:22:40 +0530 section 5/180,3/180 & 185 of Mv Act was filed against the driver and owner of the offending vehicle before concerned criminal court while four separate DARs were filed in respect of four victims before this Tribunal. 5. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3. 6. Despite opportunity, no reply or written statement was filed by Respondent no.1 and 2. In its reply filed by the insurance company, a statutory defence of breach of insurance policy has been taken. It has been pleaded that the driver of the offending vehicle was under the influence of alcohol as his blood report reveals 290mg/100ml of alcohol for which Section 185 Mv Act has also been invoked by the police. It is also pleaded that such driver of the offending vehicle was driving without a valid driving licence, for which Section 3/181 Mv Act and Section 5/181 Mv Act has been invoked by the police . It is thus pleaded that the insurance company is not liable to compensate the petitioners. Opp. 3) Relief. texts.facts: was filed against the driver and owner of the offending vehicle before concerned criminal court while four separate DARs were filed in respect of four victims before this Tribunal. 5. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3. 6. Despite opportunity, no reply or written statement was filed by Respondent no.1 and 2. In its reply filed by the insurance company, a statutory defence of breach of insurance policy has been taken. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He deposed on the lines of the Dar claiming that on 06.11.2023 at about 7:30 a.m, he was going to Kailash Colony by bus. He stopped at bus stop near Adhehini Red Light. When he was crossing red light at Brt Road alo ng with 2-3 other women, a gray color car bearing n o.DL-12CR-7508, came at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner and hit him. Due to this, victim fell on the road. An unknown person called PCR. Victim was removed to AIIMS Trauma Center where he was medically examined. PW-1 further deposed that he was working as a medical attendant at Nursing Beauro and earning of Rs.20,000/- per month. He relied upon his Adhar card as Ex.PW1/1. Complete DAR as Ex.PW1/2 and his Voter ID as Ex.PW1/3. He was duly cross examined by counsel for insurance company. Respondent no.3 /insurance company also led its evidence by examining one Daksh Arora as R3W1/1 who tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R3W1/A. He relied upon insurance policy as Ex.R3W1/1, notice issued u/O 12 Rule 8 CPC as Ex.R3W1/2, postal receipts as Ex.R3W1/3 and Ex.R3W1/4. He was duly cross examined by learned counsel for petitioner. As already discussed, insurance company is liable to compensate the petitioners. The compensation will be payable in the first instance by the insurance company/respondent no.3 with with simple interest @ 7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of DAR till actual realization and with liberty to recover the same jointly and severally from the driver and owner of the vehicle i.e. respondent no.1 and 2. In case, the interest of petitioners were stopped or excluded during the present inquiry proceedings, same is liable to be adjusted from the total interest calculated on the Award amount. In compliance of directions issued vide order dated 16.11.2021 by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Writ Petition Civil No.534/2020 titled as Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Union of India the award amount shall be deposited with State Bank of India, Saket Court Branch, New Delhi by way of RTGS/NEFT/IMPS in account of MACT PARKING FUND, A/c No. 00000042706875094, IFS Code SBIN0014244 and MICR code 110002342 under intimation to the Nazir in the prescribed format i.e. MCOP Number on the file of (Claims Tribunal Name) Date of award, Compensation Amount, Income Tax Deduction at Source, Bank Transaction Reference No./Unique Transaction Reference (UTR) Number. In turn, the State Bank of India, Saket Courts Branch shall receive the deposited sum and capture the above information and furnish a MACT no.454/2024 Harish Salikram Soni vs. Vinay & ors.
texts.arguments: (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 13. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam Insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. It has been observed by Hon'ble Madras High Court in The Branch Manager, New India Assurance Company vs. A Sathish (CMA(MD) No.653 of 2025 and CMP (MD) No.10343 of 2025, decided on 10.07.2025) that notwithstanding the deletion of proviso to old Section 149(4) of MV Act (New Section 150), The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal can order pay and recover. 16. Now as regards the issue of quantum of compensation, this court relies upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011)1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC wherein it has been observed that MACT no.454/2024 Harish Salikram Soni vs. Vinay & ors. 18.6. It was observed by Apex Court in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability --Item (ii) (a). 17.7. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 7.5% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. On such deposits being made, the insurance company shall submit a letter to the Nazir of this Tribunal enclosing a copy of the said bank advice, in prescribed format as above, as per which the deposit made to the bank account of this Tribunal, to enable this Tribunal to keep tab on the deposits made and the MCOPs for which they were made. The Hon'ble Delhi High Court vide orders dated 07.12.2018 & 08.01.2021 in FAO No. 842/2003 under the title Rajesh Tyagi & Ors. Vs. Jaivir Singh & Ors. has given the following directions: "(i) The bank shall not permit any joint name to be added in the saving account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimants i.e. saving bank accounts of the claimants shall be an individual saving bank account and not a joint account. (vi) The bank shall make an endorsement on the passbook of the claimant to the effect, that no cheque books and/or debit card have been issued and shall not be issued without the permission of the Court and the claimant shall produced the passbook with the necessary endorsement before the Court for compliance." 26. However, in a recent judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India titled as Parminder Singh vs Honey Goyal on 18 March, 2025 in S.L.P. (C) No. 4484 OF 2020 has held that : "17. 29. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will Harish Salikram (Dar) vs Vinay (291/23Gk) on 16 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36598268/ 12 ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. Even in the case of literate persons, the Tribunals are automatically ordering investment of the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit without recording that having regard to the age or fiscal background or the strata of the society to which the Harish Salikram (Dar) vs Vinay (291/23Gk) on 16 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36598268/ 13 claimant belongs or such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks it necessary to direct such investment in the larger interests of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded to him.
